questions.question_text: Which of these is **not** a surd?

options.why: Assumed the smallest number in the list must be the perfect square; $45$ lies between $36$ and $49$.
Chose an odd number as though odd numbers were perfect squares; $47$ is prime.
Picked a number close to $49$ without checking which one is exactly $7^{2}$.

questions.solution_text:
$7\times7=49$, so $\sqrt{49}=7$, a whole number and therefore rational.
$45$, $47$ and $51$ are not perfect squares, so those three roots are surds.
$\sqrt{49}$ is not a surd.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a surd?

options.why: Overlooked that $5^{3}=125$, so this cube root is the whole number $5$.
Overlooked that $3^{4}=81$, so this fourth root is the whole number $3$.
Took a large number under the root as a sign of irrationality; $12^{2}=144$.

questions.solution_text:
$3^{3}=27$ and $4^{3}=64$, and $27<50<64$, so $50$ is not a perfect cube.
$\sqrt[3]{50}=3.68403\ldots$, which never stops and never repeats.
$\sqrt[3]{50}$ is a surd.

questions.question_text: Which of these expressions is a surd?

options.why: Assumed any expression containing a root sign is a surd; $\sqrt{9}=3$, so this equals $12$.
Did not check the root first; $\sqrt{100}=10$, so this equals $6$.
Assumed a root inside a fraction stays irrational; $\sqrt{64}=8$, so this equals $2$.

questions.solution_text:
$5$ is not a perfect square, so $\sqrt{5}=2.23606\ldots$ is irrational.
Subtracting it from $4$ gives $1.76393\ldots$, which still never stops and never repeats.
$4-\sqrt{5}$ is a surd.

questions.question_text: Using a calculator, approximate $\sqrt{17}$ to $2$ decimal places.

options.why: Rounded up even though the third decimal digit in $4.123105\ldots$ is $3$.
Rounded to one decimal place and then added a zero instead of rounding to two decimal places.
Divided $17$ by $2$ instead of taking its square root.

questions.solution_text:
$\sqrt{17}=4.123105\ldots$
The third decimal digit is $3$, so round down.
$\sqrt{17}\approx4.12$ to $2$ decimal places.

questions.question_text:
Kai says $\sqrt{81}$ is a surd because it has a root sign.
Which reply is correct?

options.text: $\sqrt{81}=9$, a whole number, so it is rational and not a surd.
$\sqrt{81}$ is a surd because $81$ is an odd number.
options.why: Tests whether the number is odd instead of whether it is a perfect square.

options.text: $\sqrt{81}$ is a surd because its decimal never stops.
options.why: Assumes every root has an endless decimal, but $\sqrt{81}=9$ terminates immediately.

options.text: $\sqrt{81}$ is not a surd because $81$ is bigger than its own square root.
options.why: Compares the sizes of $81$ and $9$ rather than checking whether $81$ is a perfect square.

questions.solution_text:
$9\times9=81$, so $81$ is a perfect square.
$\sqrt{81}=9$, a whole number, so the root is rational.
A root sign alone does not make a surd; for a whole-number radicand, the number under it must not be a perfect square.

questions.question_text:
How many of these are surds?
$\sqrt{8},\ \sqrt{100},\ \sqrt[3]{9},\ \sqrt[3]{216}$

options.why: Counted $\sqrt{8}$ only, missing that $9$ is not a perfect cube so $\sqrt[3]{9}$ is also irrational.
Counted $\sqrt[3]{216}$ as a surd without checking that $6^{3}=216$.
Assumed every expression with a root sign is a surd, ignoring the perfect powers.

questions.solution_text:
$\sqrt{100}=10$ and $\sqrt[3]{216}=6$ are whole numbers, so they are rational.
$8$ is not a perfect square and $9$ is not a perfect cube.
So $\sqrt{8}$ and $\sqrt[3]{9}$ are surds, giving $2$ surds.

questions.question_text: Classify $\sqrt{-13}$ as a surd, rational, or not real.

options.text: Not real, because it is the square root of a negative number.
Surd, because $13$ is not a perfect square.
options.why: Ignored the negative sign and tested rationality before checking whether the root is real.
Classified the radicand instead of the root.
Moved the negative sign outside an even-index root, although $\sqrt{-13}$ is not real.

questions.solution_text:
The index $2$ is even and the radicand is negative.
$\sqrt{-13}$ is not real, so it is neither rational nor a surd.

questions.question_text: Which of these is a surd?

options.why: Assumed a fractional radicand always gives a surd; this root equals $\frac{5}{8}$.
Treated a square root of a negative number as irrational, although it is not real.
Assumed zero under a root sign gives a surd; this root equals the rational number $0$.

questions.solution_text:
$\frac{13}{49}$ is in simplest form. Its denominator is a perfect square, but its numerator is not, so it is not the square of a rational number.
$\sqrt{\frac{13}{49}}$ is a surd.
$\sqrt{\frac{25}{64}}=\frac{5}{8}$ and $\sqrt{0}=0$ are rational, while $\sqrt{-36}$ is not real.

questions.question_text:
Each of these roots has an odd index and a negative number underneath.
Which one is a surd?

options.why: Assumed a negative number under a cube root always gives a surd; $(-3)^{3}=-27$, so the root is $-3$.
Treated the minus sign as making the root irrational; $(-1)^{3}=-1$, so the root is $-1$.
Assumed a fifth root must be irrational; $(-2)^{5}=-32$, so the root is $-2$.

questions.solution_text:
The index is odd, so a negative number under the root is allowed in each option.
$(-3)^{3}=-27$ and $(-4)^{3}=-64$, and $-30$ lies between them, so $-30$ is not a perfect cube.
$\sqrt[3]{-30}=-3.10723\ldots$, which never stops and never repeats, so it is a surd.
